idea.body: Most triangles have no right angle, so SOHCAHTOA does not apply, and two laws cover them instead. The law of cosines is c squared equals a squared plus b squared minus 2ab cosine C. It finds a side from two sides and the angle between them, or an angle from all three sides. The law of sines, a over sine A equals b over sine B, finds a side or angle from a matched pair. A rover drives 3 meters, turns 60 degrees, then drives 8 meters. The law of cosines gives the distance back to the start. 3 squared plus 8 squared minus 2 times 3 times 8 times 1/2 is 49, so that distance is 7 meters. The area from those sides is one half times 3 times 8 times sine 60, which is 6 sqrt(3) square meters.

workedExample.prompt: A triangle has sides 7 and 15 meters with a 60 degree angle between them. Find the third side.
steps: The angle between the two known sides is given, so the law of cosines applies.
c squared equals a squared plus b squared minus 2ab cosine C.
That is 7 squared plus 15 squared minus 2 times 7 times 15 times cosine 60 degrees.
Cosine of 60 degrees is 1/2, so c squared is 49 + 225 - 105, which is 169.
The third side is the square root of 169, which is 13 meters.

figure.alt: A triangle with sides 7 and 15 meters and a 60 degree angle between them, and the third side 13 meters.

ways.name: Pick the law from what is known
ways.when: Use this first: two sides and the angle between them mean the law of cosines.
steps: A triangle has sides 5 and 8 meters with a 60 degree angle between them.
Two sides and the included angle are known, so the law of cosines applies.
c^2 = 49, so the third side is sqrt(49), which is 7 meters.

ways.trap: Using the law of sines when no matched side-angle pair is given yet.

ways.name: Draw and label, then match sines
ways.when: Use this when an angle is matched with its own opposite side.
steps: Angle A is 30 degrees opposite side a = 10 meters, and angle B is 90 degrees.
Draw the triangle and label the known angle, its opposite side, and the second angle.
The matched pair a and sin(A) sets up a/sin(A) = b/sin(B).
10/sin(30 degrees) = b/sin(90 degrees), so b = 10/(1/2) times 1, which is 20 meters.
ways.example: Angle A = 30 degrees, side a = 10 meters, angle B = 90 degrees. Find side b.
ways.trap: Matching a side with the wrong angle instead of its own opposite angle.

frames.caption: Find side b: angle A 30, a=10, B=90.
Angle A 30, side a=10 m, angle B 90.
Draw the triangle; label the angle and sides.
Matched pair sets up a/sin(A) = b/sin(B).
b = 10/sin(30) x sin(90), which is 20 m.

ways.name: The area formula
ways.when: Use this when the question asks for area instead of a side or angle.
steps: A triangle has sides 6 and 10 meters with a 30 degree angle between them.
The area formula is one half times two sides times the sine of the angle between them.
ways.example: Sides 6 and 10 meters with a 30 degree angle between them. Find the area.
ways.trap: Using a side that is not adjacent to the given angle in the formula.
